finding.title: BackfillReconciler re-enqueues 12 permanently-under-covered symbols every 20 minutes forever; minCoverage assumes an untrue fact about new listings
finding.symptom: 're-enqueued 12 under-covered' is reported identically on every pass; the same 12 symbols can never reach the threshold.
finding.evidence:
worker_runs, backfill-reconciler at 06:03, 06:27 and 06:43 UTC all report 're-enqueued 12 under-covered'.
The 12 (symbol, stream, 1d bar count, 1m bar count):
  EA 0 1907 0 | SPCX 1 61 19678 | SKHY 0 43 18469 | CBRS 0 81 13337 | FINA 0 44 40 |
  SNDQ 0 96 18868 | SPCH 0 60 17642 | SPCF 0 60 9905 | ALPXW 0 35 9 | NXGLW 0 1175 60 |
  BKYI 0 45 721 | MVO 0 1900 0
Six of them (SPCX, SKHY, CBRS, SNDQ, SPCH, SPCF) are recent listings whose 43–96 daily bars ARE their complete history — SPCX is 'Space Exploration Technologies Corp. Class A Common Stock' with 61 sessions. EA and MVO are delisted (last daily bar 2026-08-04 and 2026-07-24) so their 1m count is 0 and can never rise.
backfill.go:121-123: 'a brand-new symbol has ~500 daily bars, so anything under 100 means history never landed. const minCoverage = 100'.
Each enqueue runs BackfillDaily (2y window) + BackfillMinuteSince (30d, the live SIGNALDECK_1M_RETENTION_D per /api/datastats retention.bars1mDays=30) + a full-history Rollup(1m→1h, from=0) in backfillAndPrime.
finding.root_cause: minCoverage is an absolute bar count with no notion of a symbol's listing date or delisting date, and the comment it rests on ('a brand-new symbol has ~500 daily bars') describes a symbol added to a mature listing, not a genuine new issue. The code acknowledges persistent re-surfacing as 'the honest outcome' (backfill.go:126-127), which is right for a broken symbol but wrong for a symbol whose history is simply short.
finding.user_impact: No wrong number reaches a user, but ~864 redundant full daily+minute re-fetches per day burn free-tier Alpaca requests, and each one re-writes tens of thousands of rows plus a full-history rollup into a 5.4 GB WAL database — churn that competes with the gap-fill budget check (gapFillBudgetOK) it shares a pass with, and noise that hides a symbol whose history genuinely failed to land.
finding.proposed_fix: Compare coverage against what the symbol could have: skip when the symbol has bars back to (or near) symbols.added_at / its first available session, and skip 1m coverage entirely for symbols with delisted_at set. Both fields already exist on the symbols table.

verdict.counter_evidence:
I tried to refute this and could not. What I ran and read:

1. CODE (matches, with one bad line cite). daemon/internal/pipeline/backfill.go:121-123 is verbatim "minCoverage is the 'clearly backfilled' floor; a brand-new symbol has ~500 daily bars, so anything under 100 means history never landed. / const minCoverage = 100". Lines 128-152 are the Run loop: need := nDaily < minCoverage, OR'd with nMin < minCoverage for md.Stocks, then unconditional r.BF.Enqueue(s). No cooldown, no per-pass cap, no delisted_at check — in direct contrast to the gap-fill leg 20 lines below it (backfill.go:172-183) which DOES have gapFillPerPass=6 and gapFillCooldown=24h. The cited "backfill.go:194" is wrong: 194 is blank; BackfillMinuteSince is called at backfill.go:205, and Rollup(..., from=0) at backfill.go:87.

2. REACHABLE IN THE RELEASE CONFIG. Registered at daemon/cmd/signaldeckd/run.go:264 (&pipeline.BackfillReconciler{St: st, BF: backfiller}). Not quarantined, not a worktree copy. It is running on the live daemon now.

3. REPRODUCED THE 12 INDEPENDENTLY. I re-implemented the reconciler's own predicate as a read-only query (mode=ro URI, LIMIT-bounded count subqueries) and got exactly the same 12 symbols the auditor names, same bar counts: EA (1d>=100, 1m 0), SPCX 61/19678, SKHY 43/18469, CBRS 81/13337, FINA 44/40, SNDQ 96/18868, SPCH 60/17642, SPCF 60/9905, ALPXW 35/9, NXGLW 1175/60, BKYI 45/721, MVO (1d>=100, 1m 0). Not a copied claim — my own query.

4. NON-CONVERGENCE CONFIRMED, AND OLDER THAN CLAIMED. All 20 retained worker_runs rows for backfill-reconciler (2026-09-10 01:05 -> 07:23 UTC, spanning revisions d08d3f1, b84670c9, 5890cb99) report "re-enqueued 12 under-covered" — distribution Counter({'12': 20}), no other value. dq_events shows backfill errors for SKHY, SNDQ, SPCF, SPCH, SPCX and ALPXW dated 1787642115 (2026-08-25), i.e. the same set has been cycling for at least 16 days, not "since 06:03 today".

5. CHURN IS REAL, NOT INFERRED. dq_events contains 'backfill: prime expectancy: database is locked (5) (SQLITE_BUSY)' from this exact path. /api/datastats reports bars = 11,265,635 rows total; the 12 symbols hold ~116,700 1m rows, re-upserted 72x/day ~= 8.4M row-upserts/day, i.e. ~75% of the whole bars table re-written daily off 12 names.

6. NO LATER FIX. git log 5890cb9..HEAD -- daemon/internal/pipeline/backfill.go daemon/internal/store/ returns nothing. The daemon being 3 commits behind is irrelevant here.

WHERE THE FINDING IS WRONG OR OVERSTATED (why I corrected it down rather than confirming as written):

a) Root cause misattributed for 2 of the 12, and already documented in-repo. EA and MVO fail on the MINUTE leg (1m = 0), not the daily floor, because they stopped trading (last 1d bar 2026-08-04 / 2026-07-24). MVO literally has symbols.delisted_at = 2026-07-24 AND active = 1. daemon/internal/maintain/maintain.go:632-640 already names this exact root cause and its blast radius: "1,868 permanently-delisted rows carry active=1 at all: the delisting detector writes symbols.delisted_at but never clears `active` ... so roughly 45 callers of ListSymbols(ctx, true) — every scorer, poller and trainer in the fleet, not only this auditor — iterate the dead. Repairing the universe is the real fix and it does not live in this function." BackfillReconciler is one of those ~45 callers. That half of the finding is a known, documented, accepted condition with a named fix site elsewhere — not a backfill.go defect.

b) Contradicts stated design intent for that same half. backfill.go:125-127: "A persistently unbackfillable symbol (delisted, bad pair) keeps surfacing here and on the quality page — which is the honest outcome, not a hidden one." The author explicitly signed up for delisted names re-surfacing forever.

c) The Alpaca free-tier cost claim does not survive arithmetic. fetchBarsPage sets limit=10000 (alpaca/client.go:254), so a 2y daily pull is 1 page and a 30d minute pull is 1-2 pages: ~3 HTTP requests per backfill, ~2,600/day for all 12. Alpaca free tier is 200 req/min (~288k/day). That is under 1% — real, but not a burn. I also found no rate limiter in the Alpaca client, so nothing throttles it either way.

d) "Competes with the gap-fill budget check (gapFillBudgetOK)" is wrong. gapFillBudgetOK is a STORAGE-headroom check (gapFillBudgetMarginMB = 512MB, backfill.go:313). The re-enqueued 12 upsert idempotently inside retention and add ~no net storage, so they do not consume that budget. The two loops do not compete for it. They do compete for the SQLite write lock — which is the SQLITE_BUSY evidence above, and is the accurate version of the complaint.

WHAT GENUINELY SURVIVES: for the 6 live recent listings (SPCX 61, SKHY 43, CBRS 81, SNDQ 96, SPCH 60, SPCF 60 daily bars, every one of them still printing through 2026-09-09) plus ALPXW/NXGLW/FINA/BKYI, minCoverage=100 as an absolute bar count is unsatisfiable, and the comment it rests on ("a brand-new symbol has ~500 daily bars") is factually false for a genuine new issue. Those 10 can never converge, and no code path anywhere consults added_at or delisted_at to say so.
verdict.reasoning:
Not refuted on facts — I reproduced the exact 12-symbol set from the live DB with my own query and confirmed the identical worker_runs message across all 20 retained passes, so the mechanism is real, reachable in the shipping config, and older than the finding says (at least 16 days, per dq_events from 2026-08-25).

But the finding is right for the wrong reason on part of its own evidence, and its impact case does not hold up. Two of the 12 (EA, MVO) are the already-documented "delisted rows keep active=1" condition — maintain.go:632-640 names it, sizes it at 1,868 rows and ~45 ListSymbols(ctx,true) callers, and says the fix lives in universe repair, not here; and backfill.go:125-127 explicitly declares persistent re-surfacing of delisted names to be intended honest behavior. So the auditor's framing ("minCoverage assumes an untrue fact about new listings") explains only the other 10. The cost case is worse: with limit=10000 per page each backfill is ~3 requests, so all 12 cost ~2,600 Alpaca requests/day against a ~288k/day free-tier ceiling — under 1%, not a burn — and the claimed competition with gapFillBudgetOK is a category error, since that gate measures storage headroom and idempotent in-retention upserts add ~no storage. The real cost is write-lock contention, which I did find evidence for (a 'prime expectancy: database is locked (SQLITE_BUSY)' dq_event from this path) plus ~8.4M row-upserts/day, about 75% of the 11.27M-row bars table, re-written daily off 12 names.

Severity stays low. Nothing user-visible is wrong: no forecast, no published number, no broken journey, no untraceable input. It is background waste plus a monitoring line that can never reach zero — which makes a genuinely-failed backfill harder to spot, but that is a future-noise cost, not a launch defect. The honest one-line fix if anyone touches it is to make the floor relative to what the vendor actually has (skip when delisted_at is set, and when a re-fetch returned no new bars) rather than an absolute 100; that is a post-launch cleanup, not a gate.

Caveat on the shared context: the working tree no longer matches the brief. git HEAD is 9e0de99 (not 19a2977) and git status shows 6 modified files (Dockerfile, daemon/internal/pipeline/ai.go, ops/accuracy-registry.sh, ops/docker-entrypoint.sh, ops/ledger-provenance.sh, ops/test-ledger-provenance.sh) plus an untracked daemon/internal/pipeline/ai_transient_test.go — not the single ops/ledger-revisions.txt I was told to expect. I touched nothing; flagging it because another session is evidently editing this tree concurrently.

finding.title: /lab/track-record renders the publication REFUSAL as "TOO EARLY TO GRADE" and promises the numbers unlock in ~0 trading days
finding.symptom: The page whose stated job is "the honest scoreboard" attributes the withheld figures to a thin sample. It renders the headline "TOO EARLY TO GRADE", the counter "3652/30 independent (symbol, trading day) resolutions", a 100%-full progress bar captioned "the skill numbers below stay withheld until this bar fills", the sub-line "win rate, Brier & IC unlock in ~0 trading days (estimate)", and a chip whose tooltip reads "Too few independent resolutions to claim skill yet". None of that is why the numbers are withheld, and the sample is 122x over the floor it claims to be under.
finding.evidence:
GET /api/track-record (live, bearer auth):
  "gated": true,
  "independentN": 3652, "minIndependentN": 30,
  "distinctDays": 33, "minDistinctDays": 10,
  "gate": { "threshold": 30, "remaining": 0, "estDaysToUngate": 0, "estimate": true, ... },
  "note": "the accuracy grader has REFUSED since 2026-09-09T16:49:48 — figures over this graded window are withheld until it clears"

daemon/internal/api/trackrecord.go:190-195 is what set gated:
  if reg.RefusedSince != nil && *reg.RefusedSince != "" {
      gated = true
      collapseReason = "the accuracy grader has REFUSED since " + *reg.RefusedSince + ...
  }

web page, line 266-271:
  {current.gate == null
     ? (current.note ?? "not yet significant")
     : current.gate.estDaysToUngate == null
       ? "unlock ETA unknown..."
       : `win rate, Brier & IC unlock in ~${current.gate.estDaysToUngate} trading day...`}
`gate` is non-null in the live payload, so `current.note` — the only field carrying the real reason — is never rendered.

line 286 width: `${Math.min(100, (3652 / 30) * 100)}%` = 100%; line 292-294 caption: "the skill numbers below stay withheld until this bar fills."
line 151 tooltip: "Too few independent resolutions to claim skill yet — numbers withheld."
finding.root_cause: `gated` is an overloaded boolean: it means either "below the evidence floor" or "the grader refused". The page assumes the first meaning everywhere. The daemon passes the discriminating reason in `note`, but the UI only reads `note` on the `gate == null` fallback branch, which never fires when the gate block is present.
finding.user_impact: On the product's own honesty scoreboard, a hard publication refusal (23 collapsed cross-sections over 83 graded day-horizons) is presented to the reader as a transient sample-size wait that clears tomorrow. /accuracy, / (landing), /proof and the home ProofStrip all correctly show REFUSED with the collapsed-cross-section explanation, so the same withholding is described four different ways across the app and the worst description is on the page a sceptical reader is most likely to open. The page also contradicts itself on screen: a 100%-full bar under the sentence "withheld until this bar fills".
finding.proposed_fix: Have the daemon send a discriminant (e.g. `gateReason: "refused" | "insufficient"`) or, without a backend change, treat a non-empty `current.note` as authoritative: when `note` is present render <RefusalNotice status="REFUSED" reason={current.note}/> in place of the TOO EARLY block (the component already exists and is used by /proof and ProofStrip), suppress the progress bar and the estDaysToUngate sentence, and change the chip tooltip from "Too few independent resolutions" to the note text. Independently, the "unlock in ~N days" sentence should not render when independentN already clears gate.threshold.

verdict.counter_evidence:
I tried to refute this on five fronts and failed on all five.

1. CODE SAYS WHAT IS CLAIMED — verified by my own reads (not the auditor's quotes).
`sed -n '245,300p' web/src/app/lab/track-record/page.tsx` shows verbatim:
  line 257: TOO EARLY TO GRADE
  lines 259-263: {current.independentN}/{current.gate?.threshold ?? current.minIndependentN} independent (symbol, trading day) resolutions
  lines 266-271: `current.gate == null ? (current.note ?? "not yet significant") : current.gate.estDaysToUngate == null ? "unlock ETA unknown..." : `win rate, Brier & IC unlock in ~${current.gate.estDaysToUngate} trading day...``
  line 287: width: `${Math.min(100, (current.independentN / (current.gate?.threshold ?? current.minIndependentN)) * 100)}%`
  line 293-294: "the skill numbers below stay withheld until this bar fills."
`sed -n '100,175p'` shows line ~111 `const gated = current?.gated ?? true;` and the chip title at ~150-152: "Too few independent resolutions to claim skill yet — numbers withheld."
`grep -n -i "note|refus|collaps" page.tsx` returns exactly ONE render of `current.note` — line 268, on the `gate == null` branch. There is no refusal banner anywhere else on the page (I read lines 176-256: PagePurpose, ErrorState, Skeleton, four StatTiles, RegimesLivePanel, RegimeMissesPanel — none mentions the grader refusal).
daemon/internal/api/trackrecord.go:188-202 reads exactly as claimed: `if reg.RefusedSince != nil && *reg.RefusedSince != "" { gated = true; collapseReason = "the accuracy grader has REFUSED since " + ... }` — the same `gated` boolean the two evidence floors set at line 165.

2. LIVE PAYLOAD CONFIRMS THE BAD BRANCH IS THE ONE THAT FIRES. My own call, GET http://127.0.0.1:8322/api/track-record (bearer, HTTP 200):
  gated=True, rawN=87116, independentN=3652, minIndependentN=30, distinctDays=33, minDistinctDays=10, winRate=None, brier=None, ic=None
  note='the accuracy grader has REFUSED since 2026-09-09T16:49:48 — figures over this graded window are withheld until it clears'
  gate={"threshold":30,"remaining":0,"estDaysToUngate":0,"estimate":true,"accrual7d":{...}}
`gate` is NON-NULL, so `note` is unreachable; `estDaysToUngate` is 0 (not null), so the string that renders is literally "win rate, Brier & IC unlock in ~0 trading days (estimate)". Bar width = min(100, 3652/30*100) = 100%. Both evidence floors are cleared 122x and 3.3x over — nothing about the sample is thin, yet every word on screen says it is.

3. NOT DEAD / NOT QUARANTINED / NOT A .claude WORKTREE COPY. `git diff --stat HEAD -- web/src/app/lab/track-record/page.tsx` is empty, so the file is at HEAD (HEAD is now 9e0de99, advanced past the 19a2977 in the brief by a concurrent session; the page file is NOT among the modified files). The string ships in the built client bundle: `grep -rl "TOO EARLY TO GRADE" web/.next/static` -> web/.next/static/chunks/0gbs9aq6dm0g3.js. The route serves: `curl -o /dev/null -w %{http_code} http://127.0.0.1:8323/lab/track-record` -> 200. It is one of the most-linked pages in the app: web/src/app/lab/sections.ts:56, components/CommandPalette.tsx:72, components/FirstRunTour.tsx:37, components/home/ProofStrip.tsx:26 and :183, components/home/TodaysRead.tsx:258, components/NextStep.tsx:76/103, components/health/HealthBoard.tsx:439, lib/goal.ts:72 ("See how accurate we've been").

4. NO GUARD, NO LATER COMMIT. Last commit touching the page is ab715e1; nothing after it addresses this. There is no fallback that surfaces `note` when `gate` is present — I grepped the whole web/src for `estDaysToUngate` and only this page and the type in lib/api.ts:2305 use it.

5. DOES NOT CONTRADICT A SETTLED VERDICT — it IS the check the brief ordered. The settled verdict says the refusal is the honesty machinery working and "DO check that the refusal is represented consistently and honestly everywhere (registry -> API -> UI -> docs)." I confirmed the divergence myself: GET /api/accuracy returns HTTP 503 with {"status":"REFUSED","grader_fresh":false,"reason":"grader has been refusing since 2026-09-09T16:49:48: publication gate: the graded window contains 23 collapsed cross-section(s) of 83 day(s): 1d 2026-07-27 (6 distinct across 330 symbols), ..."}, and web/src/app/accuracy/page.tsx:372/405 renders REFUSED/REFUSED_STALE explicitly. Same withholding, two contradictory explanations, and the wrong one is on the page the nav calls "See how accurate we've been".

The only point in the finding I could not independently confirm is the exact wording on /proof and the landing ProofStrip (I confirmed /accuracy handles REFUSED explicitly and that /api/accuracy 503s with the collapse reason; I did not read /proof's rendered copy). That does not change the defect.
verdict.reasoning:
Confirmed, not refuted, at the claimed severity.

The page does not publish a bad number — the StatTiles correctly show "withheld" for win rate, Brier skill and IC. What it publishes is a bad REASON and a false forward promise, and that is the thing this launch is defined to block on ("misleading/unsupported user-visible claims"). "win rate, Brier & IC unlock in ~0 trading days (estimate)" is a concrete claim that is false: the grader refusal is orthogonal to the accrual counter, so no amount of accrual clears it. The countdown will read ~0 days indefinitely.

The root cause is real and is a one-boolean overload, exactly as reported: trackrecord.go sets `gated` from three unrelated conditions (indepN floor, distinct-day floor, grader REFUSED / collapsed window) and ships the discriminator only in `note`. The UI reads `note` on the one branch that cannot fire while a `gate` block exists. The daemon comment block at lines 167-187 shows the author already fought this exact "refused on one document, published on six" divergence and closed it on the DATA side — the payload is now honest — but the presentation side was never updated to read the new field, so the fix landed in the API and stopped at the component.

Why blocker and not high: the failure is concentrated on the single page whose stated purpose is "Our scorecard... a number with no sample behind it is worse than no number," it is reachable from the home proof strip, the first-run tour, the command palette and the goal picker, and it contradicts /accuracy — which any sceptical reader will also open — within one click. It also contradicts itself on screen: a 100%-full progress bar directly above the sentence "the skill numbers below stay withheld until this bar fills," plus a chip whose tooltip says "Too few independent resolutions" next to a chip reading "3,652 independent". A reader who notices that concludes either the site is broken or the withholding is being spun. For a product whose entire proposition is disclosing what it cannot claim, that is worse than the refusal itself.

Fix is small and belongs in the component, not the API: when `note` is present, render it as the reason and suppress the countdown/bar/tooltip (or have the daemon emit a `gateReason` discriminator so the UI stops inferring "thin sample" from a bare `gated`). Preferably the latter, since /proof, ProofStrip and the desk recommendation card read the same payload and any of them could make the same inference later.

finding.title: /lab/honesty hero tiles render mean forward return 100x too small and label the score-ordered buckets "Best"/"Worst"
finding.symptom: The two hero tiles pass the raw 0-1 fraction `meanFwd` straight into StatTile with suffix="%", so they render "0.01%" and "-0.00%" while the QuintileTable a few hundred pixels below renders the identical numbers as "+1.31%" and "-0.42%". The tiles also assume buckets[4] is the best-performing bucket and buckets[0] the worst; the array is ordered by SCORE bucket, and on the live data the ordering is inverted.
finding.evidence:
GET /api/honesty?horizon=1d (live):
  buckets[0] = {label:"strong sell", meanFwd: 0.01306615638395247, n:356}
  buckets[4] = {label:"strong buy",  meanFwd: -0.004204010736426009, n:799}

page.tsx:157-167:
  <StatTile label="Best Quintile"  value={current.buckets?.[4]?.meanFwd} decimals={2} suffix="%" glow="up" />
  <StatTile label="Worst Quintile" value={current.buckets?.[0]?.meanFwd} decimals={2} suffix="%" glow="down" />
Kit.tsx AnimatedNumber: display.toLocaleString(undefined,{minimumFractionDigits:2,maximumFractionDigits:2})
  => (-0.004204).toLocaleString(...) === "-0.00"  -> renders "-0.00%" in GREEN under "Best Quintile"
  => ( 0.013066).toLocaleString(...) === "0.01"   -> renders "0.01%" in RED under "Worst Quintile"

Every other consumer of the same field multiplies first:
  QuintileTable.tsx:68  fmtPct(b.meanFwd * 100)
  HeroStats.tsx:104     fmtPct(spread * 100)
  track-record/page.tsx:562  fmtPct(m.meanFwd * 100)
  signal-backtest/page.tsx:377,494  fmtPct(res.meanFwd * 100)
finding.root_cause: Two unit conventions for a field named `meanFwd` (0-1 fraction from /api/honesty and /api/track-record; already-in-percent from /api/market-memory), and StatTile's `suffix` prop does no conversion. Separately, the tile indices hard-code an assumption that the score-ordered quintiles are monotone in forward return — the very assumption this page exists to test, and which the live data refutes.
finding.user_impact: The hero band of the page titled "HONESTY — How wrong have we been?" states a 100x-understated forward return and colours the worst-returning bucket green as "Best Quintile". Its own quintile table contradicts it on the same screen. The file's own comment at line 159-161 says a "0.00%" here would be "a fabricated forward return, on the page whose entire purpose is not fabricating them" — the units bug produces exactly that.
finding.proposed_fix: Multiply at the call site (`value={b.meanFwd != null ? b.meanFwd * 100 : undefined}`) exactly as QuintileTable/HeroStats already do, and derive the tiles from the data rather than fixed indices — pick max/min of `buckets.filter(b => b.n > 0 && Number.isFinite(b.meanFwd))` by meanFwd and label them with `b.label` (e.g. "Best bucket — strong sell"), so an inverted ordering shows up instead of being asserted away.

verdict.reasoning:
I could not refute it. I read the cited lines myself and re-ran the live call, and both halves of the claim hold at current HEAD.

Units bug: page.tsx:162,170 pass the raw 0-1 `meanFwd` into StatTile with suffix="%", and StatTile's only formatter (Kit.tsx:67, AnimatedNumber -> toLocaleString with min/maxFractionDigits) applies no conversion. Every other consumer of the identical array multiplies by 100 first (QuintileTable.tsx:68, HeroStats.tsx:105, track-record/page.tsx:562, signal-backtest 377/494). The tiles and the table are handed the SAME object (`<QuintileTable buckets={current.buckets ?? []} />`, page.tsx:185), so one consumer converting and the other not is definitive, not inferred.

Index/label bug: buckets are score-ordered (live labels run strong sell -> strong buy), and glow="up"/"down" are hard-coded to indices 4/0. `.glow-up` is `var(--bid)` green (motion.css:57), applied unconditionally regardless of the value's sign. On live data the strong-buy bucket is NEGATIVE, so the green "Best Quintile" tile is affirmatively claiming edge in the bucket that lost money. Even under the charitable reading that "Best Quintile" means "best-scored bucket" rather than "best-returning", the unconditional green/red colouring is still wrong-signed.

Two corrections to the finding, neither refuting: (1) the auditor's specific numbers did not reproduce - live values are now 0.020494/-0.002133 with n 349/632, not 0.01306/-0.004204 with n 356/799; data has moved, shape is identical. (2) QuintileTable sits inside <ProOnly> (page.tsx:181) and is collapsed in the default SIMPLE mode, so the "contradiction a few hundred pixels below" is literal only in PRO mode. However HeroStats is NOT gated and renders immediately beneath the tiles with `fmtPct(spread * 100)` = -2.26% in red, sub-labelled "strong buy minus strong sell mean forward return" (HeroStats.tsx:52-62,103-113). The same-screen self-contradiction therefore exists in the default view as well - this strengthens rather than weakens the finding.

Reachability: the file is clean vs HEAD (git diff --stat empty; note HEAD has moved to 9e0de99 since the brief's 19a2977, and 11 other files are now dirty - a concurrent session is committing - but neither page.tsx nor Kit.tsx is among them). Route registered in lab/sections.ts:57 and CommandPalette.tsx:55; no web/src/middleware.ts exists so /lab is not edge-gated. Not quarantined, not a .claude/worktrees copy. No guard, default or caller intervenes - StatTile's own null-guard (hasData, Kit.tsx:150) only catches missing values, not wrong units.

No settled verdict is implicated: this is not the IC verdict, the auto-retired directional model, or the publication-gate refusal. It is a presentation-layer units/index defect on a page whose stated purpose is not fabricating forward returns - and the file's own comment at page.tsx:159-161 warns about exactly the "0.00%" output the bug produces.

Severity high is justified, not inflated: public unauthenticated route, hero band, states a 100x-understated return and colours the losing bucket green as "Best", contradicted on the same screen by the panel beneath it. finding.root_cause: The 2026-08-02 nav consolidation moved the page component from /signals/alerts to /market/activity and carried the old route metadata over verbatim (the layout comment says so: "Carried over from /signals/alerts"), but the page that landed at the new route is a plain event timeline, not the alerts surface those four components composed. Nothing re-checked the description against what the new page actually renders, and nothing flags an unimported component, so the subtree went dead silently.
finding.user_impact: The description is what a search engine, a link preview and a shared URL show. It advertises the product's honesty machinery — "cites its published rule", "gated below minimum sample size" — for a page that shows neither, which is a claim the shipped page does not support. Separately, a real measured feature (forward returns after each alert kind, with explicit gating flags, n=600 for anomaly_vol) is computed and served but is unreachable to any user.

Do not leave the description as-is. Add a cheap guard so this class cannot recur: a test that asserts every route's metadata nouns are backed by a rendered testid, or at minimum a lint rule failing on components under web/src/components that nothing imports.
finding.repro: curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8323/market/activity | grep -o '<meta name="description" content="[^"]*"'  — then open /market/activity and look for an outcomes table or a rule citation. Neither exists; the page renders PageHero + 4 StatTiles + a timeline.

verdict.reasoning:
The central factual claim survives: web/src/app/market/activity/layout.tsx:11 serves a description promising an outcomes table of measured forward returns, and the page at that route renders no such table. I read all 258 lines of page.tsx and web/src/app/market/layout.tsx (HubTabs + children only) — the rendered output is PageHero + 4 StatTiles + kind-filter chips + a timeline of row.detail. The four named components are genuinely unimported, and /api/alert-outcomes genuinely has no app consumer. So refuted=false.

But three of the finding's supporting arguments are wrong, and they are what inflated it to "high":

1. IMPACT REFUTED. The claimed harm is "what a search engine, a link preview and a shared URL show." The served robots.txt contains `Disallow: /market/` and sitemap.xml lists only 6 public pages (/, /accuracy, /proof, /volatility, /glossary, /health). /market/activity is deliberately excluded from crawling and from the sitemap. No search engine surfaces this description. Only a manually pasted link preview would.

2. SURFACE IS AUTH-GATED. There is no web/src/middleware.ts, but the page's own data fetch 401s for anonymous users and renders ErrorState "Sign in to see activity" with hint "Activity is scoped to your account — log in." A shared link is not a marketing surface for a stranger.

3. HALF THE CLAIM IS SUPPORTED. "every alert cites its published rule" is substantially true of what actually renders. Live /api/alerts details carry the rule and threshold inline ("z=-2.8 vs the means of 10 trailing 5m windows across a 60m baseline — descriptive statistic, not a prediction"), and the published rulebook (ALERT_RULES from components/signals/alerts/rules.ts) IS rendered, on /welcome page.tsx:20,366. Only the "outcomes table" clause is unsupported by the shipped page.

4. ROOT CAUSE REFUTED. The auditor blames the 2026-08-02 nav consolidation (250863a). `git show --stat 250863a` for that path shows 1 file, 2 insertions, 2 deletions — comment text only. The description already existed verbatim in 91da5c4. The actual regression is d0e39b7 ("Web v4 Cinematic Terminal redesign across every tab"): d0e39b7^:page.tsx imports MethodologyPanel and OutcomesPanel at lines 24-25 and renders them at 183/186; d0e39b7's version has neither. The description was accurate until the redesign rewrote the page.

5. NO RUNTIME OR BUNDLE IMPACT. grep for the dead components' distinctive strings ("withheld (min N)", "unpublished rule") across web/.next/static and web/.next/server returns nothing — unimported modules are tree-shaken and never reach a client. The orphaned endpoint 401s anonymously and has Go tests (daemon/internal/api/alertoutcomes_test.go), so it is neither a security nor a correctness hazard.

No settled verdict is contradicted — this is not about the accuracy gate, directional IC, dircall, starvation or loop cadence.

Residual defect worth fixing: one clause of one meta description asserts a feature the shipped page does not have, on a product whose positioning is honesty about its own claims. That is real debt (delete the clause, or re-mount OutcomesPanel and delete the other three orphans), but it is a one-line copy fix on a noindexed, login-gated internal tab. Low, not high, and not release blocking.

2. I read all 291 lines of web/src/app/market/unusual/page.tsx. All seven names in web/src/components/signals/unusual/ (CompoundLane, MagnitudeBar, MethodologyPanel, SeverityBadge, SummaryStrip, UnusualTape, measure) have zero references anywhere in web/src outside that directory. (The one MethodologyPanel hit is a different file, web/src/components/signals/alerts/MethodologyPanel.tsx.) The subtree really is orphaned.

The backend has no compound concept either, so the page could not render it even if it wanted to: GET /api/anomalies returns flat rows (id/symbol/market/ts/kind/z/detail/measure/value/proxy) with no compound field, and every "compound" hit in daemon/*.go is return-compounding (confluence, backtest CAGR), unrelated.
5. Reachable in the release configuration: the route is in the market nav (web/src/app/market/layout.tsx:26) and CommandPalette.tsx:36, and next.config.ts:46 307s /signals/unusual into it.
6. Not fixed by a later commit. layout.tsx was last touched by 250863a (the merge the comment names); the component dir by 6108a66. Nothing after.
7. No settled verdict is involved — this is not IC, the grading gate, dircall, starvation, or loop cadence.

WHERE THE AUDITOR OVERSTATES — the two halves of this finding have very different weight:

The dead directory contributes ZERO user impact and should not carry severity. I checked the actual production build (BUILD_ID 6CDcEfoiMeWZHpRzd3k0r, .next/server/app + .next/static): neither "compoundGroups" nor CompoundLane's "co-occurrence, not causation" string appears anywhere in it. Only .next/dev turbopack chunks carry them. Nothing from that directory ships. It is repository tidiness, not a launch concern.

The stale description is real but its entire user-facing surface is one <meta name="description"> tag — search snippets, link previews, crawlers. It is not on-page copy. The page's own visible copy (PageHero subtitle: "Things that look odd today... Odd is a place to start looking, not a signal on its own") is accurate and appropriately hedged, and the API's own note/proxyNote render honestly. So a reader on the page is never told compound signals exist; only a search result or shared link is.

That is genuinely an unsupported user-visible claim on a launch candidate, so it should be fixed — but it is a one-sentence copy edit with no data, security, traceability or journey consequence. Medium overstates it; low is right. Not release-blocking on its own.

1) Cited code says what is claimed. Each of the six files contains only its own `export default function <Name>` and (for three of them) a comment naming itself. A repo-scoped Grep of web/ for all six names (excluding node_modules/.next/.claude) returns exactly 9 lines, and every one of them is either the definition itself or a self-referential comment inside the same file. There is not a single `import` of any of the six anywhere.

2) Reachable? No — that is the point of the finding, and it cuts both ways. There is no `web/src/app/predict/` route at all (I listed all 59 page.tsx files and the app/ directory), so the predict/ explainer pair has no route to be reached from. These modules are never pulled into a bundle.

3) Not handled elsewhere. web/eslint.config.mjs is just `eslint-config-next/core-web-vitals` + `/typescript` with no unused-export or knip-style rule, so the auditor's "lint does not flag it" is correct. tsconfig `include` is `**/*.tsx`, so tsc still typechecks these files — meaning they compile cleanly and the build will never surface them either. Nothing catches this.

4) Root cause substantiated, with one date slip. web/next.config.ts really does carry the comments the auditor cites: line 19 "2026-07-19 nav consolidation (9 tabs -> 5)", line 28 "2026-07-18 hub merge: MARKETS + SIGNALS -> one MARKET hub", line 31 "2026-08-02: the merge is now COMPLETE in the source tree too", line 33 the "which one do I edit?" phrase. The auditor wrote "2026-08-02 hub merge"; the config dates the hub merge 2026-07-18 and 2026-08-02 as when it completed in the tree. Cosmetic, not a refutation. The supersession story is independently corroborated by git: FusionExplainer.tsx's last commit (a7a53b1, 2026-07-02) shipped a `/predict` route that no longer exists in app/.

The auditor's cross-check that /market/signals renders SignalScoreHero (line 8, rendered line 97) and FactorTiles (line 10, rendered line 118) also verified exactly as quoted.

7) No settled verdict is contradicted. Nothing here touches directional IC, the accuracy publication gate, dircall, starvation, or research-loop cadence. I also scanned the dead files for claim-shaped content: the only numbers are "50% coin-flip" axis labels in PredictionGauge and ProbHistogram. No accuracy or edge claim is baked into any of them, so there is no dormant misleading claim waiting to be re-mounted.

For a public-launch RC the entire cost is that a reviewer might read a superseded file as shipped. That is real but sub-"low" in a release taxonomy. "low" is not inflated in any dishonest way; this is a hair-split, and the finding is honestly scoped and correctly self-limited.

refuted_titles.title: NEXT_PUBLIC_SIGNALDECK_PUBLIC and NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL are build-time-only, the Dockerfile web build declares no ARG for either, and the release plan tells the operator to set them at runtime
refuted_titles.why:
The finding's mechanism is half-real, but its central user-impact claim is contradicted by a file the auditor imported and then did not read, and half its file evidence no longer matches the tree. Severity is inflated from high to low.

1. THE IMPACT CLAIM IS FALSE — this is the decisive refutation and it holds regardless of the Dockerfile.
The claim is "AuthGate therefore sends every anonymous visitor to /login instead of /" and "the honesty pages (/accuracy, /proof) are unreachable to visitors." AuthGate.tsx imports isPublicRoute on line 6 and calls it on line 33; line 37 is `if (onLogin || ready) return;` — the effect exits before the fetch, so the redirect the auditor quotes (lines 61-63) is never evaluated on a public route, and line 75 renders children. web/src/lib/publicRoutes.ts:17-27 lists "/", "/accuracy", "/proof", "/volatility", "/glossary", "/health", "/login". Every single page named in the impact claim is on that list. The auditor quoted lines 56-64 of AuthGate and stopped short of the guard, 25 lines above, that makes its own quoted line unreachable for the pages it says are broken.
What actually degrades with the flag undefined: an anonymous visitor who hand-types or bookmarks a PRIVATE route (/dashboard, /lab/*, /hud) gets /login instead of /. robots.ts:19 disallows every one of those prefixes, and Shell.tsx:429-440 renders public chrome with PublicNav only, so no link on the public site leads there. That is a cosmetic difference on a deep link into a page the visitor has no business seeing — not "the exact broken public journey."

2. HALF THE FILE EVIDENCE IS STALE. The claimed "Dockerfile stage 2 in full: 43-49" and the claimed repro output ("grep -n NEXT_PUBLIC Dockerfile fly.toml -> only NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED") match commit 19a2977 but not the tree. The working tree Dockerfile carries ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL="" / ENV at lines 57-58 under an 8-line comment (49-56) stating the exact build-time-inlining rule the auditor says nobody enforced. Note also that the claimed grep output is impossible on its own terms: a grep for NEXT_PUBLIC cannot match NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED.
Important caveat, stated plainly: git diff HEAD shows those 10 lines are UNCOMMITTED. The brief said the tree had one modified file (ops/ledger-revisions.txt); it actually has ten modified files plus an untracked test. So the auditor most likely read the committed state honestly and a repair agent patched it afterward, in this same session. Limb A of the finding was therefore real at the audited commit and is now partly remediated.

3. THE SURVIVING KERNEL IS SMALL. NEXT_PUBLIC_SIGNALDECK_PUBLIC genuinely has no ARG anywhere — confirmed. A repo-wide grep (excluding .claude/, node_modules/, .next/) finds exactly two code readers: AuthGate.tsx:63 (refuted above) and proof/page.tsx:38, a "use client" component where PUBLIC_MODE only selects the wording of an error hint at lines 209-215 — whether operator remediation copy ("start signaldeckd (:8322)", "open public reads with SIGNALDECK_PUBLIC_READS") is shown. Undefined means a public visitor sees operator-flavored copy on an ERROR path. That is a minor copy leak, not a broken journey and not a misleading accuracy claim.

4. THE LIVE "PROOF" IS THE FALLBACK WORKING. robots.txt/sitemap.xml on 8323 do return localhost — I reproduced it — but web/.env.local does not exist (only web/.env.example), so this build never had NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL set. site.ts:10-13 and Dockerfile:52-56 both say the localhost fallback is deliberate precisely so it looks obviously-local rather than plausibly-right. It is evidence the designed fallback fires, not evidence the container path is broken. And "unindexable" overstates it: a cross-domain sitemap is ignored by crawlers, it does not block indexing — the robots.txt Allow list and internal links still work.

5. A DIFFERENT, SMALLER DEFECT IS REAL and the auditor missed it. The newly added Dockerfile comment asserts "ops/docker-build.sh forwards it; DEPLOY.md tells the operator to set it." Both are false against the current tree: ops/docker-build.sh (unmodified, at HEAD) passes only --build-arg GIT_REV plus "$@", and grep for NEXT_PUBLIC in DEPLOY.md returns nothing. That is an unverified fix comment, worth flagging separately at low severity — but it is not the finding under review.

No settled verdict is implicated; this is a config/docs issue, not an accuracy-gate or directional-model one.

refuted_titles.title: SIGNALDECK_ASSUME_TUNNEL fails OPEN on an unrecognised value, contradicting the codebase's own fail-closed boolean rule
refuted_titles.why:
The CODE claim is accurate — I confirmed the exact text at daemon/internal/config/config.go:479-482 (`if v := strings.TrimSpace(os.Getenv("SIGNALDECK_ASSUME_TUNNEL")); v != "" { return v == "1" || strings.EqualFold(v, "true") }`) and boolEnv's opposing doc comment + `envcfg.Reject` call at config.go:339-364. It is also true that daemon/internal/health/health.go:269 and :384 surface envcfg rejections, so boolEnv's refusals ARE visible while this branch's are not. To the auditor's credit they even understated it: the early return short-circuits BEFORE the allowlist-derived publication check at config.go:499-503, so an unrecognised value also disables the platform-independent signal that was added specifically because the A9 fix regressed twice.

But the finding fails on reachability, on its documentation claim, and on its stated root cause.

REACHABILITY — no shipped configuration can hit it. (a) The container release path never lets an operator supply this value: Dockerfile:133 `ENTRYPOINT [... /usr/local/bin/docker-entrypoint.sh]`, and ops/docker-entrypoint.sh:34 unconditionally `export SIGNALDECK_ASSUME_TUNNEL=1` — a recognised spelling, hardcoded, overwriting anything set in fly.toml [env]. (b) fly.toml sets `SIGNALDECK_PUBLIC_READS = "1"` explicitly anyway, so PublicReads on the public deployment never comes from `private` at all. (c) The live local daemon's daemon/.env sets SIGNALDECK_PUBLIC_READS=false and SIGNALDECK_OPEN_SIGNUP=false explicitly, and boolEnv gives an explicit value precedence over the default; GET /api/health on the running daemon returns `"openSignup":false`. The claimed scenario needs an operator to simultaneously (i) hand-type a spelling outside the two documented ones, (ii) bind loopback, (iii) run a tunnel the allowlist does not name, and (iv) ignore both .env.example and ops/GO-LIVE.md:42, which tell them to set SIGNALDECK_PUBLIC_READS=false explicitly.

DOCUMENTATION — the auditor quotes .env.example:187-189 as presenting the var as a generic authoritative override, but the quoted line enumerates exactly the two accepted spellings: `"1"/"true" forces the open defaults CLOSED`, with the example line `# SIGNALDECK_ASSUME_TUNNEL=true`. I grepped every .md and .example in the repo (excluding .claude/) and nothing anywhere suggests `yes`/`on` for this variable. Code and documented contract agree; the "yes is accepted everywhere else" argument is a plausible-typo argument, not a contract violation.

ROOT CAUSE — "should have used boolEnv" is wrong in direction and the auditor half-notices this then asserts it anyway. boolEnv fails closed to FALSE; here false IS the open direction. Dropping boolEnv in unchanged reproduces the exact bug. So the finding also misprescribes the fix.

Not a settled-verdict conflict — this is genuinely separate from the IC/grading/dircall verdicts. It is a real latent robustness gap in an operator-facing override that fails silently in the open direction, worth a one-line fix (treat any non-empty unparseable value as `true` and route the refusal through envcfg.Reject so it appears in health alongside its siblings), but it is not a launch blocker and "high" is inflated.

refuted_titles.title: SIGNALDECK_ALLOW_DIRTY_BUILD is tested by presence, so setting it to 0 or false DISABLES the provenance gate
refuted_titles.why:
The auditor read the code correctly — main.go:87 and :110 do presence-test, and daemon/.env values do reach os.Environ before the gate, so `SIGNALDECK_ALLOW_DIRTY_BUILD=0` would indeed enable the override. That mechanical claim survives. What does not survive is everything that makes it a finding.

It is not a defect: presence-testing is the consistent, documented idiom for the entire provenance-override family — three git hooks use shell `[ -n ]`, the PowerShell provenance gate uses `$null -ne` and its comment states it deliberately honours "the SAME override the daemon does". boolEnv is reserved for the security toggles where a misparse opens a door. Treating one member of a mirrored convention as a parsing slip is the auditor misreading intent.

It is not reachable: the gate branch requires a dirty or unstamped build, and the release path builds from `git archive HEAD` with an explicit ldflags stamp. The live daemon returns modified:false, resolvable:true, and the key is absent from daemon/.env. Both preconditions would have to be created by hand.

And the impact is inverted: the "+dirty" suffix is deliberately welded into the row stamp so the grader cannot miss it, and accuracy_registry.revision_resolvable() permanently refuses exactly those rows. The override cannot launder ungradable rows into a published number — it produces rows the honesty machinery rejects. The .env.example line the auditor quoted as evidence ("nothing downstream can tell afterwards") is the documentation being more pessimistic than the code.

What remains is a one-line documentation nit: .env.example should say any non-empty value enables the override (or the gate should adopt killswitch.envHalt's explicit-off parsing, which already exists in-repo at daemon/internal/killswitch/killswitch.go:114-134 and is the natural model). That is low, post-launch polish. Nothing here should stop a public launch.

refuted_titles.title: web/.env.example is gitignored and untracked — the web tier's env template does not exist in any clone, and the root .env.example points at it
refuted_titles.why:
The git mechanics are real but the defect is not. Three of the finding's load-bearing claims are false, and the remedy it implies would make the release worse.

1. "the web tier's two server-side variables" — FALSE. `grep -rn "process\.env\.SIGNALDECK_API_TOKEN" web/src web/next.config.ts` returns NOTHING. The web tier never reads that variable. It has ONE server-side variable, SIGNALDECK_DAEMON. Half the missing template documents a key the code does not consume.

2. "A public-launch clone cannot discover SIGNALDECK_DAEMON without reading route.ts" — FALSE. Three TRACKED files name it: web/README.md:18 (the "one architectural rule" section, the first place anyone reads), Dockerfile:107, fly.toml:27.

3. Zero functional impact on a cold clone. All four consumers default to the exact string the template would supply — `process.env.SIGNALDECK_DAEMON || "http://127.0.0.1:8322"` at web/src/app/api/[...path]/route.ts:14, web/src/app/page.tsx:38, web/src/app/accuracy/page.tsx:332, web/src/app/volatility/page.tsx:49. A clone with no web/.env.local behaves identically to one with the template filled in.

4. The untracked file is WRONG, not merely absent — tracking it is an anti-fix. web/.env.example:7-8 describes SIGNALDECK_API_TOKEN as "Bearer token the server-side proxy attaches when talking to the daemon." web/src/app/api/[...path]/route.ts:66-74 says the exact opposite, deliberately, with the rationale: "Deliberately do NOT attach SIGNALDECK_API_TOKEN here... an ANONYMOUS visitor was handed admin." Tracked web/README.md:19-22 states the same rule. Committing this file would ship a public-launch instruction to put an admin-mapped credential into the web tier for a proxy that never reads it — on the single security boundary this repo documents most carefully. Correct remedy is deleting the stray local file, not adding a `!.env.example` negation.

5. Contradicts documented release policy. docs/PUBLIC_RELEASE_PLAN.md:50, under "Never include": "`daemon/.env`, `web/.env.local`, any `.env*`." web/.gitignore:34's unnegated `.env*` is consistent with that; the auditor's "stock create-next-app file, never given the negation" root cause is an unverified story about intent, and `git log --all -- web/.env.example` is empty, so nothing ever regressed.

Residual, genuinely info-grade: the parenthetical "(see web/.env.example)" at .env.example:19 dangles in a clone. One stale cross-reference in a comment.

REDIRECT — the auditor pointed at the wrong half of this pair. The tracked, public-facing .env.example CONTRADICTS ITSELF about this token. Lines 18-20: "put the SAME value in web/.env.local as SIGNALDECK_API_TOKEN (see web/.env.example) — the Next.js /api/* proxy route reads it server-side". Lines 164-167: "Bearer token for NON-BROWSER callers... Never send it from the browser proxy — doing so hands admin to anonymous visitors." route.ts:66 and web/README.md:19 confirm lines 164-167 are the truth and lines 18-20 are stale. That is a misleading security instruction in a tracked file a public deployer will read. Still not release-blocking (failure mode is a dead env var, not an exposure — the proxy ignores it either way), but it is the actual defect in this neighborhood and worth a one-line fix at .env.example:18-20.

refuted_titles.title: 82 of 128 daemon environment variables are undocumented, including every retention key the code itself classifies as CRITICAL for data deletion, and SIGNALDECK_PUBLIC_SURFACE
refuted_titles.why:
The headline claim — "82 of 128 daemon environment variables are undocumented, including every retention key ... and SIGNALDECK_PUBLIC_SURFACE" — is false. The repro measures absence from ONE file (.env.example) and the finding reports it as absence from documentation. Every family the finding names as undocumented is documented elsewhere, in the doc a reader would actually consult:

1. RETENTION KEYS ARE DOCUMENTED. STORAGE.md carries two tables covering all 13: lines 33-45 (per-table policy, e.g. "| `bars` 1m | **60 days** | `SIGNALDECK_1M_RETENTION_D` | compact -> 1h + archive raw -> prune |") and lines 165-179, a dedicated env-var table of name / default / meaning. The finding's own "one of them is in live use" example collapses on this: daemon/.env sets SIGNALDECK_1M_RETENTION_D=30, and STORAGE.md:166 names that exact key with its `60` default. So the live deployment depends on a documented key, not an undiscoverable one.

2. THE ENVCFG QUOTE IS A GUARD, QUOTED AS IF IT WERE THE DEFECT. The auditor cites envcfg.go:20-26 as proof that a mistyped retention window silently deletes data. Reading the whole comment (lines 1-31) inverts that: the silent-fallback shape is the hole this package CLOSES. "This package only makes the divergence visible ... those keys are recorded as CRITICAL (RejectCritical) and make the fleet unhealthy rather than merely being logged." The dangerous-mistype scenario the finding builds its severity on is the scenario envcfg was written to catch. Item 3 of my brief — "already handled by a guard" — applies directly.

3. SIGNALDECK_PUBLIC_SURFACE IS DOCUMENTED AND FAILS CLOSED, AND WHEN ON IT RESTRICTS. Documented at docs/PUBLIC_RELEASE_PLAN.md:7, :11, :31 and :35 (that last one is step 3 of the deploy sequence — the deployer's checklist), README.md:168, and exercised end-to-end in audits/2026-09-08-release-reaudit.md (F20). config.go:129-148 adds 20 lines of in-code rationale. Substantively, the finding has the direction backwards: the field comment says it "turns the anonymous-read rule from a DENYLIST into an ALLOWLIST," and security.go:285-300 confirms the allowlist answers first and nothing below can widen it. An operator who never finds this flag gets the pre-existing denylist behavior — the flag is a hardening opt-in, not an exposure switch. Its absence from a daemon .env template is not a security hole.

4. RISK AND PAPER FAMILIES ARE DOCUMENTED TOO. RISK_POLICY.md:168, 205, 237-238, 269, 301-303 names SIGNALDECK_RISK_MAX_POSITION_WEIGHT, MAX_GROSS_EXPOSURE, MAX_SECTOR_WEIGHT, MAX_POSITIONS, MAX_CORR_TO_BOOK, MAX_DRAWDOWN, FLATTEN_DRAWDOWN and MAX_DAILY_LOSS with their in-force values. EXECUTION_SPEC.md:185, 190-191 names SIGNALDECK_PAPER_BARRIERS and both barrier ATR knobs.

5. THE DOCKERFILE VARS ARE HANDLED BY THE CALLER, AND THE CITATION IS WRONG. SIGNALDECK_LOG_FILE and SIGNALDECK_REGISTRY are set at Dockerfile:105-109, not 95-99 as cited. The container sets them; no operator has to. That is the textbook "handled by a caller."

6. THE HEADER DOES NOT CLAIM WHAT THE FINDING SAYS IT CLAIMS. Also miscited: the header is at .env.example:129-133, not 125-128. Read literally, it says the undocumented set "included every switch that decides whether this daemon is exposed. That is the gap this section closes." The gap named is the exposure-switch gap, and the section then documents ROOT, DB, HTTP, ALLOWED_HOSTS, WEB_ORIGINS, API_TOKEN, PUBLIC_READS, OPEN_SIGNUP, TRUST_PROXY, ASSUME_TUNNEL, TV_WEBHOOK_SECRET and the local workspace key. It never claims to document all 120. "The template's own header claims this gap is closed" is a misreading of which gap.

7. OPS-SCRIPT VARS ARE OUT OF SCOPE. .env.example:1 states its scope: "SignalDeck daemon config — copy to .env and fill." SIGNALDECK_ANCHOR_REPO, SIGNALDECK_TOOLS, SIGNALDECK_TRASH etc. are ops-script knobs, not daemon config, so counting them against a daemon template inflates the number.

WHAT SURVIVES (why low, not info): two small true things. The header's "120 SIGNALDECK_* variables exist in the code" is a present-tense number that has drifted to 128 — a stale figure in a shipped file on a repo that sells measured claims. And .env.example contains no cross-reference to STORAGE.md / RISK_POLICY.md / EXECUTION_SPEC.md (grep for "retention|STORAGE.md|RISK_POLICY|EXECUTION_SPEC|docs/" returns only line 253, an unrelated sentence about backup size). A one-line "see STORAGE.md for retention windows, RISK_POLICY.md for risk gates" pointer would close the real gap. That is a docs-polish item, not a medium.

Not release-blocking: no data corruption (envcfg guards the deletion keys), no security hole (PUBLIC_SURFACE defaults false and only narrows), no misleading user-visible claim (the honesty surface is untouched), no broken journey. Does not touch any settled verdict.

refuted_titles.title: The fleet-quiesce drain has NEVER succeeded: 724 of 724 recorded attempts timed out, so every WAL checkpoint pays a 30-second fleet-wide pause and then runs against live readers anyway
refuted_titles.why:
The mechanical observations are real, but the statistic that carries the finding is invalid and the user-impact conclusion is inverted. What survives is a low-severity tuning nit, not a high-severity defect.

CONFIRMED. quiesceDrainTO = 30s (workers.go:75) vs minRunTimeout = 15m (workers.go:73). The drain loop polls r.running every 50ms and breaks on the deadline; `grep -c 'cancel()'` over lines 593-684 returns 0 — it genuinely never cancels. Stream workers (deadline.IsZero()) are excluded by design. The dq_events counts reproduce exactly: 724 / 724 / 0. And by my own independent measurement the drain really does time out essentially always — all 18 completed storage-governor passes in the worker_runs retention window (2026-09-09 07:53 -> 2026-09-10 07:23) produced a quiesce_stall row, and every one reads "(quiesced, N attempts)" with N>1, i.e. the quiesced first TRUNCATE attempt returned Busy every single time.

REFUTED — 1. The "0/724 success rate" is selection bias, not a measurement. workers.go:663 writes the dq row ONLY when `stat.DrainTimedOut || stat.Drain > quiesceDrainWarn` (5s). A drain finishing under 5s writes no row at all, so `timedOut=false` is only reachable in the narrow 5-30s band. The denominator is "stalls", not "attempts". The auditor's headline number cannot support the claim it is used for; the conclusion happens to be near-right, but only via my measurement, not theirs.

2. This is the load-bearing error: `TRUNCATE 0/0 frames` is SUCCESS, read as failure. Of the 18 completed passes, 16 report `TRUNCATE 0/0 frames (quiesced, N attempts)` with no BUSY suffix and `wal=0.0MB` on disk — the WAL fully checkpointed and truncated to zero. Only 2 (02:05, 05:25) say `BUSY — WAL NOT truncated`. The claim "the WAL reclaim it exists to enable still fails (TRUNCATE 0/0 frames on most passes)" is exactly backwards: 16/18 reclaimed the WAL completely.

3. "The pause buys nothing / reclaim fails" is refuted by the system's own alarms. `wal_checkpoint_starved` = 0 events ever and `wal_checkpoint_ineffective` = 0 events ever — those two dq kinds (maintain.go:1130, :1241) exist precisely to fire when the reclaim genuinely stops working. Neither has fired once. `wal_checkpoint_busy` last fired 2026-09-08 06:41, none in the two days since.

4. The freeze is far smaller than implied and already bounded by design. The retry loop that actually wins the TRUNCATE runs OUTSIDE the window: QuiesceDo returns after fn + 3s, and maintain.go's retryLoop executes after it returned. The comment at maintain.go:1017-1019 says so explicitly — "the retries run UNQUIESCED so nothing else is held up while it waits." Fleet gate per pass is drain(<=30s) + one pragma + 3s, not the 64-1930s run duration.

5. The impact arithmetic is misleading. 724 x 30s = 6.0h over the 38-day event range is a 0.66% duty cycle, charged against a fleet whose shortest run deadline is 15 minutes. The finding cites no worker that missed a deadline because of it.

6. The WAL CRITICAL attribution is wrong. maintain.go:820-830 documents this exact phenomenon from a live measurement — a deploy took the WAL 38 MB -> 861 MB in four minutes while the governor was asleep, and SQLite's own autocheckpoint reclaimed it to journal_size_limit, not the governor and nothing to do with the drain. The log's last entry (825.3 MB) is from a file last written 2026-09-09 16:48; the WAL on disk right now is 64.0 MB, exactly the 64 MB journal_size_limit. The spike self-reclaimed.

7. "Nothing is cancelled, so the doc comment is false" misreads the comment. workers.go:574-576 says the drain is bounded "so a worker that ignores cancellation must not be able to block the window forever" — the WINDOW is bounded, which is true as written. Cancelling in-flight runs to force a drain would abort research/forecast/ingest work mid-write, which is strictly worse for a system whose value is a complete forecast record. Not cancelling is intended.

WHAT ACTUALLY SURVIVES (low): since the quiesced first attempt has never won in the retained window and the win always comes from an unquiesced retry, quiesceDrainTO = 30s is largely dead weight. Lowering it, or dropping the quiesce around the first attempt entirely, would remove ~30s of fleet gating per hourly pass at no measured cost. That is a tuning change for after launch, not a blocker.

Not release-blocking: no data corruption, no security hole, no misleading user-visible claim, no broken user journey, no forecast-traceability gap. The WAL sits at its configured limit and the two genuine failure alarms have never fired.

refuted_titles.title: /api/health - the endpoint both the Fly check and the Docker HEALTHCHECK probe - does a per-worker query over worker_runs on every request, so the liveness probe goes down with the database it is meant to report on
refuted_titles.why:
The mechanism is real but the causal claim is falsified by the auditor's own evidence source.

WHAT IS TRUE: /api/health does two SQLite reads before branching on the caller. daemon/internal/api/api.go:485 (GetMeta for schemaContract) and api.go:502 `failing, werr := d.failingWorkers(r.Context())`, which at api.go:593 calls RecentWorkerRunsPerWorker(ctx, 20). Line numbers are off by one from the finding (580 -> 580 is right for the func; 592 -> 593; 526 -> 527; 554 -> 555) but the substance is accurate. Dockerfile:114 and fly.toml:49 do probe /api/health at the stated intervals/timeouts.

WHAT IS FALSE — the core causal claim ("any event that blocks readers, the VACUUM, makes the probe fail"): I pulled every api-probe run inside the VACUUM window. storage-governor started its run at 05:25:13 UTC and ran 1930s, ending 05:57:23, with detail `... db=5195.9MB wal=64.0MB vacuumed=true`. /api/health answered HTTP 200 on ELEVEN consecutive probes inside that whole-file VACUUM of the 5.2 GB database: 05:25:58, 05:27:31, 05:29:31, 05:31:31, 05:33:31, 05:35:31, 05:37:31, 05:41:32, 05:42:25, 05:43:31, 05:57:22. Health did not go down with the VACUUM. It survived the single worst reader-blocking event in the retained history.

TIMING KILLS THE ATTRIBUTION: the one api-probe error started at 05:25:12 — one second BEFORE the storage-governor VACUUM run started (05:25:13). It sits inside a process-wide stall that began at 05:18:34, seven minutes earlier, when downsampler blew its 15-minute deadline. Nine workers that never touch /api/health hit the same 15m deadline in that window (downsampler, signal-runner, alert-runner, composite-scorer, composite-scorer-1w, anomaly-scanner, prediction-runner, outcome-resolver, dq-auditor). The probe failure is a symptom of that stall, correctly recorded; it is not evidence that health's own DB reads are the fragile part.

COST CLAIM CONFLATES TABLE WITH FILE: worker_runs holds 3326 rows across 103 workers. The window query returns 2060 rows in 20.4ms and EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN shows `SCAN worker_runs USING INDEX idx_worker_runs` — it never touches bars, which is where the 5.4 GB lives. Live /api/health latency measured 17-23ms over five samples, 22ms authed. Reader pool and writer pool are separate *sql.DB handles (store.go:120 read pool 4 conns, store.go:128 writer 1 conn), so health's read is not queued behind the writer at the Go level either.

IMPACT CLAIM IS UNSUPPORTED: Docker HEALTHCHECK is --interval=30s --retries=3, so it needs ~90s of CONTINUOUS failure to mark unhealthy; the evidence is exactly one 12-second failure in 118 api-probe runs. Docker HEALTHCHECK alone also does not restart a container. The "restart orphans in-flight worker runs" evidence cites orphan sweeps at 00:01 and 04:23 — the last `orphaned` row on 09-10 is 04:23:15, and NO orphan sweep followed the 05:25 probe failure. Those are local Windows daemon restarts on a box with no Docker or Fly in the loop; they were stitched to an unrelated event.

DELIBERATE, DOCUMENTED DESIGN: api.go:497-501 states the reason health reads fleet state ("health was a liveness probe wearing a health probe's name ... A health endpoint that cannot go unhealthy is decoration"), and Dockerfile:105-112 reasons explicitly about health-vs-ready. This is an intentional trade the code argues for, not an oversight.

RESIDUAL, HONESTLY STATED: /api/health is genuinely not a pure liveness probe, so a hypothetical reader-blocking event worse than a 32-minute VACUUM could take it down. That is a low-severity architectural note, not a blocker. I did NOT determine the root cause of the 05:18-05:25 process-wide stall — that stall is real and is a separate question from this finding.

refuted_titles.title: ops/check-grader-health.ps1 invokes bare `python` instead of the repo venv interpreter, so the ledger guard runs under whatever Python is first on the scheduled task's PATH
refuted_titles.why:
The two cited lines exist verbatim, but every load-bearing claim built on top of them is wrong or overstated, and the residual is a style nit in an ops-only script with zero user-visible surface.

1. "the interpreter every other part of this repo names explicitly" is FALSE. Every other Python call site in ops/*.ps1 uses bare `python`: overnight.ps1:79, selfimprove-loop.ps1:164-165, eighty-loop.ps1:710, test-run-captures-stderr.ps1:21. Bare `python` IS the ops-PowerShell convention here, so lines 68/147 are consistent, not inconsistent. The ops shell scripts mostly PATH-probe (`for cand in python3 python py` in accuracy-registry.sh:62, lib-portable.sh:32, signaldeck-backup-offline.sh:31, revalidate-structural.sh:52). Exactly two sites name .venv (market-close.sh:149, signaldeck-ctl.sh:268 — the auditor's own cited counter-example, and a minority of ~10 sites).

2. "a system-wide Python that is not the one the repo tests against" is FALSE. .venv/pyvenv.cfg says `home = C:\Users\Nicholas_N\AppData\Local\Programs\Python\Python312` — the venv's base interpreter IS the exact install bare `python` resolves to. Both report Python 3.12.10. There is no version skew to be exposed to.

3. "the dependency is unstated and unpinned" overstates it. tools/ledger_revision_reachability.py imports only argparse/datetime/os/sqlite3/subprocess/sys/tempfile plus sibling accuracy_registry, which itself imports only argparse/csv/datetime/hashlib/json/math/os/sqlite3/statistics/sys plus local tools/ modules. There is no third-party dependency in the transitive closure, so the venv's 407 site-packages entries are irrelevant to this path. I ran the guard under both interpreters: byte-identical stdout and identical exit 1.

4. "a context whose PATH has not been exercised since the guard was added" inverts the risk. Line 68 uses the SAME `& python` invocation and has been resolving under the identical S4U task for the whole log history — the last scheduled run (09/09 16:47:54, log mtime 16:48, LastTaskResult 1 matching the log's final 'RESULT: unhealthy') produced a parsed HEARTBEAT line, which is only reachable if `& python` ran successfully in that context. What is new at line 147 is the script being run, not the interpreter lookup, and the lookup is already proven there.

5. "the entire grader-health check dies rather than the guard alone" is wrong about ordering. Line 147 is the LAST check in the file; HEARTBEAT (line ~68-113) and WAL (line ~118-133) have already been written with Write-Output before it. A CommandNotFound there loses only the guard and the RESULT line, and it fails LOUD: $ErrorActionPreference='Stop' aborts with a non-zero exit, and ops/check-task-health.ps1 reads every SignalDeck task's LastTaskResult (lines 57-62), so the failure surfaces on the next health sweep. This is a fail-loud path, not the silent-success shape the script was written to catch.

The one true, unrefuted fact — the guard has not yet run under the scheduled task (19a2977 committed 2026-09-09 22:46:44, task last ran 2026-09-09 16:47:54, and the log's last entry carries no LEDGER REVISIONS line) — is a scheduling timing observation, not a defect in the script.

Residual: naming .venv/Scripts/python.exe at both sites would be marginally tidier. That is info-level hygiene. Nothing about it is data corruption, a security hole, a misleading claim, a broken user journey, or an untraceable forecast, and check-grader-health.ps1 ships nothing to users.

Honest limitation: I could not execute inside the real S4U task session, so PATH resolution in that context is inferred from the log/LastRun/LastResult correspondence rather than directly observed.

refuted_titles.title: Five tables and four indexes exist in the live database but are declared nowhere the Go schema contract can see, so a fresh volume gets a different schema than production
refuted_titles.why:
The raw count (105 declared / 111 live) is real and I reproduced it byte-for-byte. Every claimed consequence is wrong.

1) "Four indexes declared in no source file at all" is factually false for one of them. tools/validate_signals.py:290 creates idx_validation_advisory_run via an f-string: `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_{ADVISORY_TABLE}_run ON {ADVISORY_TABLE} (run_ts, signal)` with ADVISORY_TABLE="validation_advisory" (line 66). A literal-name grep misses it; the auditor's did.

2) "A missing index on the prediction ledger's identity lookup" — there is no such lookup. idx_prediction_ledger_ident is on (symbol_id, horizon, bar_ts). No query in the daemon filters prediction_ledger by bar_ts; bar_ts appears only in SELECT column lists. Every access is by seq (store/ledger.go:151,195; ledgeranchor.go:300; ledgercache.go:83), by COUNT(*) (backup/backup.go:238, backup/content.go:51), by predicted_at (cmd/prereg-amend/spec_revision.go:77), or by (symbol_id, horizon) ORDER BY seq DESC (LedgerFor) — which is precisely what the DECLARED idx_prediction_ledger_sym (symbol_id, horizon, seq DESC) at schema.sql:433 covers. `git log -S "idx_prediction_ledger_ident" --all` returns nothing: this index is in no commit, i.e. hand-made against the live DB, never part of any contract. Its absence on a fresh volume costs nothing.

3) idx_universe_membership_day: the repo's own audit already records it as redundant — drafts/verification_ledger_residual.json:211 "is fully redundant with the primary key's implicit index and is never chosen" (34.6 MB). Absent on a fresh volume is an improvement, not a defect.

4) "On a fresh volume it does not exist until that tool happens to run" is the documented design, and it is guarded on both sides. Every Python tool does create-then-write in the same call path: tools/forward_test.py:369 `_store_once` runs `conn.execute(SCHEMA)` on the line immediately before its INSERT; spa_ledger.py:126 and validate_signals.py:273 do the same. The ONLY Go consumer of forward_test_daily — daemon/cmd/prereg-amend/spec_forwardtest.go:64-72 — probes sqlite_master first and carries the comment "A missing table is zero, not an error: the grading tool creates it on first run, so 'not there yet' is the expected state at registration time and the only honest reading of it." That is the guard the finding says does not exist.

5) "The shell test exercises a narrower shape than production" is not a defect. sd_ft_stale_line (ops/lib-forward-test.sh:19) reads exactly one thing, `SELECT MAX(session) FROM forward_test_daily`, and the eligible column for its filter; a (session, eligible) fixture is the minimal correct fixture for that function, not a competing schema declaration. It also already handles a missing table (`2>/dev/null) || return 0` plus the empty branch).

6) research_ledger_runs and symbol_bars_epoch hold 0 rows and have no creator and no reader — the auditor concedes they are "pure dead weight." Dead weight that is absent from a fresh volume is the desired state, not a divergence with user impact.

7) sqlite_sequence is SQLite-internal (prediction_ledger.seq is INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT), not an undeclared object.

8) None of the five tables appear in SchemaContract (grep returns nothing), so no worker's boot-time readiness depends on them, and web/ has zero references to any of them — no user-facing route can 500 on their absence.

The one-directional verifySchema is deliberate, not an oversight: its own error text names the failure it guards ("a column added to schema.sql instead of to migrate() never lands on an existing DB") — the direction that silently loses writes. A symmetric check would hard-fail daemon boot on any database carrying a hand-made index, converting operator housekeeping into an outage.

Residual truth worth one line in a housekeeping note, not a release gate: three indexes on the live DB (idx_prediction_ledger_ident, idx_rledger_runs_hyp, idx_universe_membership_day) are not reproducible from any source file, and one of them wastes 34.6 MB. No query uses any of the three. Nothing here is data corruption, a security hole, a misleading claim, a broken journey, or an untraceable forecast.

refuted_titles.title: regime_changes has no dedup constraint and its guard read runs outside the write transaction: 217 (symbol_id, ts) collisions, worst case the same bar recorded flipping 12 times
refuted_titles.why:
The observable facts reproduce, but the finding's root cause, its implied remedy, and its severity are all wrong.

WHAT SURVIVES (verified myself):
- daemon/internal/store/schema.sql:184-191 — regime_changes has only `id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY` plus `idx_regime_changes ON (ts DESC)`. No unique constraint. True.
- daemon/internal/store/predict.go:417-441 — prev label is read via s.db (read pool) at :419, the tx opens on s.w at :422. True as described.
- The row counts reproduce exactly: 5574 rows, 217 duplicate (symbol_id, ts) groups, worst (531=ADA/USD, ts 1788220800) = 12 rows, ids 4915-4923 + 4956-4958, alternating range->uptrend.
- It is reachable live: GET /api/chart-overlays?symbol=ADA%2FUSD&market=crypto&days=365 on the running daemon returns 63 regime markers with 12 sharing ts 1788220800. Rendered by web/src/components/viz/BigCandle.tsx -> CandleChart overlays (dashboard + /s/[market]/[symbol]).

WHY THE ROOT CAUSE IS REFUTED — the race does not exist and produced none of these rows:
1. Single writer. The only production caller of UpsertRegime is daemon/internal/pipeline/predict.go:1364 inside RegimeRunner.Run — a serial for-loop over symbols, registered exactly once at daemon/cmd/signaldeckd/run.go:277, interval 30 minutes. Every other hit in the repo is a _test.go. There is no second caller to race against.
2. Direct empirical test. A read-outside-the-transaction race means a lost update, which necessarily leaves at least one change row whose from_lbl does not equal the previously committed to_lbl for that symbol. I ran a LAG window query over all 5574 rows: broken chain rows = 0. Every single transition links perfectly. The log is fully self-consistent — the guard read was never stale, not once.
3. The observed shape refutes it anyway. A lost update yields two identical same-direction rows; the data shows strict A->B->A->B alternation with consecutive ids. That is the signature of sequential re-classification passes each genuinely observing a flip, not a torn read.

The only real mechanism is the surviving half of the auditor's own alternative explanation: the change row is stamped with the BAR ts, so several genuine transitions within one bar collapse onto one x-coordinate.

ALREADY LARGELY FIXED, AND THE FIX IS LIVE (auditor missed it):
predict.go:1361 now calls trimFormingDaily(...) — "settled bars only (2026-09-07)", from commit ab715e1 "Repair pass 2026-09-07: settled-bar clocks". `git merge-base --is-ancestor ab715e1 5890cb9` confirms it is in the RUNNING daemon revision. With the forming bar trimmed the classifier input is fixed within a day, so re-passes no longer flip. The data agrees: of 217 duplicate groups only 14 have max(id) > 5000 and only 1 has max(id) > 5300, out of 5574 rows. The 12-row worst case (ids 4915-4923) predates the fix. Residual today: exactly ONE duplicated (symbol, ts) pair — QBTZ @ 1788840000, ids 5395/5533/5534 — in the live /api/regime top-50, and web/src/app/market/macro/page.tsx:68 slices to the top 10.

THE PROPOSED REMEDY WOULD BE A REGRESSION:
The INSERT at predict.go:434-436 has no ON CONFLICT clause. Adding UNIQUE(symbol_id, ts) would make a legitimate second same-bar transition return a constraint error; UpsertRegime propagates it and RegimeRunner.Run does `return "", err`, aborting the entire classification pass for every symbol after the flapping one. That trades stacked chart markers for a worker outage.

SEVERITY: no corrupted numbers, no fabricated claim, no security or provenance issue, nothing that publishes an unsupported figure. The rows are an honest record of what the classifier actually did. The residual user impact is cosmetic marker stacking on a handful of historical crypto chart points plus one duplicated feed row. Low, not medium; not release-blocking.

Worth keeping as a cosmetic backlog item: collapse markers sharing a (symbol, ts) in RegimeChangesForSymbol (keep first-from + last-to), or stamp the change row with wall-clock time. Not before launch.

refuted_titles.title: publication_verdicts is empty and its sticky-retirement trigger has never fired, because the only production writer sits behind the collapse gate that is currently refusing
refuted_titles.why:
The auditor's raw observations are true, but the finding is a mischaracterization on three counts, and its stated user impact is already handled by a different, populated belt.

1. THE QUOTED COMMENT IS THE FIX'S OWN CHANGELOG, READ AS A LIVE BUG REPORT. accuracy.go:241-248 is past tense: "publication_verdicts had ZERO rows and PutPublicationVerdict had no production caller ... The layer this route exists for was inert." That block was ADDED by commit 33ac417 ("Backlog: arm sticky retirement", 2026-08-12), which is an ancestor of HEAD (git merge-base --is-ancestor 33ac417 HEAD -> yes) and is present in the running revision 5890cb9 (git show 5890cb9:daemon/internal/api/accuracy.go greps PutPublicationVerdict at :259). The auditor quoted the commit that fixed the condition as evidence that the condition is current.

2. THE CLAIMED USER IMPACT IS FALSE — retirement is persisted, in evidence_claims, not only in publication_verdicts. The live DB holds directional-ensemble-1d and directional-ensemble-1w with status='retired'. publication/verdict.go:145-155 (SourceEvidence branch) sets retired=true, RetirementSticky=true and PublicationStatus RETIRED from those claims alone, independently of RetirementHistory. matchingClaims (accuracy.go:345) matches: splitPredictor turns a registry label into predictor="directional-ensemble", horizon="1d", and HasPrefix("directional-ensemble-1d","directional-ensemble") plus Contains(id,"1d") both hold. The package's own doctrine comment names three belts, not one: "Evidence retires a model, a failed interval retires a model, and history keeps it retired." History is the third belt. There is an end-to-end test that proves the belt the auditor says is un-armed is not needed for the scenario claimed: TestAccuracy_RefutedModelReadsRetiredNotInsufficient (daemon/internal/api/accuracy_test.go:94-127) asserts RETIRED + retired=true + sticky=true with publication_verdicts empty, driven purely by the evidence claim. So "a model could be re-published as if it had never been retired" does not follow for any model that is actually retired today.

3. THE STATED ROOT CAUSE IS NOT THE OPERATIVE CAUSE RIGHT NOW. data/accuracy_registry.json currently has rows: [] (n rows 0). Even with every gate deleted, `for _, rr := range reg.Rows` at accuracy.go:215 would iterate zero times and write nothing. Separately, the gate that actually fires live is the registry RefusedSince marker at :144 (the live reason begins "grader has been refusing since 2026-09-09T16:49:48"), not collapsedGradingWindow at :190 as the root cause states — the collapse text is the grader's own refusal_reason carried in the marker.

4.
